done_when: After a sync, .codex/config.toml registers every role file sync writes with its description, and sets the default subagent model and effort from forge.toml's build subagents entry when it has one, while roles the team registered by hand stay.

known.title: Gate: test_28_sync expects the obsolete role registry

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - running the configured full test suite in CI.
This change always registers every shipped role with its description, but tests/test_setup.py:167–169 still asserts exact equality with a config containing only agents.reader and no description. Consequently, tests/test_setup.py::test_28_sync fails after a successful sync, blocking the tests check. Update that assertion to accommodate the expanded registry while retaining its checks for preserved client settings.
findings.title: Gate: test_28_sync expects the obsolete role registry

why: Codex sessions opened in client repos have no registered subagent roles and no default subagent model, so their subagents run on the session's expensive model and spend tokens.
